title: AO/133/2012 of GHANPATI @ DHAPAT RAI AHUJA Vs TARUN KUMAR

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Appeal from Order No. 133 of 2012
Ghanpati @ Dhapat Rai Ahuja. ÖÖ.Petitioner.
Versus
Tarun Kumar. ......Ö. Respondent.
Present:
Mr. Lok Pal Singh, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. Arvind Vashisht and Ms. Monika Pant, Advocate for respondent.
Honíble Alok Singh, J ( Oral).
Present appeal is filed assailing the judgment and
order dated 14.02.2012 passed by Civil Judge (SD), Haridwar in
Original Suit No. 08 of 2012 whereby learned trial court was
pleased to reject the application moved by the plaintiff /
appellant, herein, seeking ad interim injunction.
Brief facts of the present case, inter alia, are that
plaintiff / appellant filed O.S. No. 8 of 2012 in the court of Civil
Judge (SD), Haridwar (Ghanpati @ Dhanpat Rai Ahuja Vs.
Tarun Kumar) seeking permanent prohibitory injunction to the
effect that defendant / respondent be restrained to make any
interference in the possession of the plaintiff / appellant in
House No. 515 consisting of five rooms on ground floor and
five rooms on first floor along with toilet, bathroom. It is stated
in the plaint that earlier Shyam Lal, son of Sohan Lal was owner
and in possession of property, in question. Shyam Lal adopted
plaintiff / appellant as son. Shyam Lal expired on 25.03.2012
and Raj Kumari, wife of Shyam Lal, adopted mother of plaintiff
/ appellant expired on 23.07.2009 and all the last rites of Shyam
Lal and Raj Kumari were performed by the plaintiff /
appellant, being their adopted son. It is further stated in the
plaint that Raj Kumari had executed a WILL on 27.06.2009 in

2
favour of the plaintiff / appellant. It is further stated that in the
year 2010, Jyoti, started claiming her title over the property, in
question, claiming herself to be daughter of Shyam Lal,
therefore, plaintiff / appellant had filed suit being O.S. No. 123
of 2011. However, during the pendency of O.S. No. 123 of 2011,
matter was settled between plaintiff / appellant and Jyoti and
as per terms of settlement, three rooms on the ground floor
were given to Jyoti and rest of the rooms at ground floor and 5
rooms on the first floor were given to plaintiff / appellant.
After the settlement, O. S. No. 123 of 2011 was withdrawn by
the plaintiff / appellant.
Application was moved by the plaintiff / appellant
seeking ad interim injunction restraining the defendant /
respondent to make any interference in the possession of the
plaintiff / appellant during the pendency of the suit.
In O.S. No. 08 of 2012, defendant / respondent has
filed his reply to the ad interim injunction application, stating
that he had purchased the entire property from Jyoti and Jyoti
was owner and in possession of property, in question and now,
defendant / respondent is owner and in possession of property,
in question. It is denied that plaintiff / appellant was adopted
by Shri Shyam Lal. It is further pleaded that Jyoti, who has sold
the property to the defendant, was real daughter of Shri Shyam
Lal.
Learned trial court, vide impugned order, was
pleased to reject the ad interim injunction application. Feeling
aggrieved, plaintiff / appellant has preferred this appeal.
I have heard Mr. Lok Pal Singh, Advocate
appearing for the appellant and Mr. Arvind Vashisht & Ms.

3
Monika Pant, Advocate for respondent and have carefully
perused the record.
Mr. Lok Pal Singh, Advocate, appearing for the
appellant submits that plaintiff / appellant is in actual physical
possession of 5 rooms on first floor and 2 rooms on the ground
floor and this can be verified by appointing an Advocate
Commissioner. He further submitted that since Jyoti was
daughter of Shyam Lal, adopted father of plaintiff / appellant,
therefore, matter was settled with Jyoti in view of the fact that
after death of Shyam Lal, Jyoti and plaintiff have inherited the
property, in question, in equal share, being adopted son and
natural daughter of Shyam Lal. As per settlement, three rooms
on the ground floor were given to Jyoti and rest of the property
was given to plaintiff / appellant. He further contended that
Jyoti neither sold entire house nor was competent to sell the
house in view of the fact that plaintiff / appellant had half
share in property and is in possession of five rooms on first
floor and two rooms on ground floor, as per settlement held
between plaintiff / appellant and Jyoti.
On the other hand, Mr. Arvind Vashisht, Advocate
for respondent submits that earlier suit no. 123 of 2011 filed by
the plaintiff / appellant was withdrawn by the plaintiff /
appellant on 11.08.2011 by moving application under Order 23
Rule 1 CPC, therefore, for the same cause of action, plaintiff /
appellant is precluded from filing subsequent (present) suit.
Earlier suit was withdrawn by the plaintiff admitting that Jyoti
was the sole owner in possession of the property, in question.
Learned counsel for the plaintiff /appellant does
not dispute that application was moved by the plaintiff /
appellant for withdrawing earlier suit no. 123 of 2011.

4
At the time of considering the ad interim injunction
application, learned court is required to see prima facie case,
balance of convenience and irreparable loss.
Since plaintiff / appellant himself admitted in
application dated 11.08.2011 moved in earlier suit that Jyoti was
sole owner in possession of the property, in question and
therefore, prima facie, plaintiff / appellant does not prove to be
owner of property in question. Consequently, no prima facie,
case in favour of the plaintiff / appellant is made out.
Learned counsel for the appellant, at this stage,
submits that in fact, settlement was arrived between the parties
to the effect that Jyoti was owner of three rooms on the ground
floor and plaintiff / appellant was owner of rest of the property
but due to fault of lawyer it could not be placed on record.
I am afraid, I cannot accept this plea, at this stage
and I have to believe whatever is written in the application
dated 11.08.2011. Since no prima facie case in favour of the
plaintiff / appellant is made out, therefore, learned trial court
rightly rejected the ad interim application.
I do not find any fault with the impugned order
rejecting the ad interim injunction application. Therefore,
appeal fails and is hereby dismissed. It is clarified that
observations made hereinbefore are only for the purpose
deciding the present appeal and the trial court shall decide suit
at its own merit, in accordance with law without being
prejudice from any observation made hereinbefore by this
Court or made in the impugned order.
 (Alok Singh, J.)
 04.04.2014
SKS
